title: What is Optional in Java 8
question: What is Optional in Java 8? What problem does it solve?
realWorldScenario: findById() returning Optional<User> forces the caller to explicitly handle the 'not found' case instead of getting an unexpected null.

title: Optional.of vs ofNullable vs empty
question: What is the difference between Optional.of(), Optional.ofNullable(), and Optional.empty()?
realWorldScenario: Use ofNullable when the value may be null; of() throws NullPointerException if null is passed.

title: orElse vs orElseGet
question: What is the difference between Optional.orElse() and Optional.orElseGet() in Java 8?
realWorldScenario: orElse(expensiveDefault()) always calls the method even if Optional has a value; orElseGet(() -> expensiveDefault()) is lazy.

title: Optional.map() and flatMap()
question: How do Optional.map() and Optional.flatMap() work in Java 8?

title: orElseThrow()
question: What does Optional.orElseThrow() do in Java 8? How is it used in REST APIs?
realWorldScenario: repository.findById(id).orElseThrow(() -> new ResourceNotFoundException(id)) is the standard Spring pattern.

title: Optional Anti-Patterns
question: What are common misuses (anti-patterns) of Optional in Java?
realWorldScenario: Using Optional.get() without isPresent() is worse than a null check; using Optional as a field type wastes memory.

title: Optional.ifPresent()
question: How do you use Optional.ifPresent() in Java 8? How is it cleaner than an isPresent() check?
realWorldScenario: optional.ifPresent(user -> sendEmail(user)) executes an action only when a value is present.

title: Optional.filter()
question: What does Optional.filter() do in Java 8?
realWorldScenario: optional.filter(u -> u.isActive()).orElseThrow() — checks a condition on the value without unwrapping it first.
